_source: Official GATE 2027 EE syllabus (data/pyq/official_pdfs/EE/EE_GATE2027_syllabus.pdf), curated by hand: topics copied verbatim and split at the syllabus's own commas/semicolons; a labelled group such as 'Network Theorems: ...' or 'DC machines: ...' is kept whole so the label stays with its items. Subject names are the syllabus's own labels, except where marked in _editorial.

_editorial.Electric Circuits: Section 2 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Electromagnetic Fields: Section 3 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Signals and Systems: Section 4 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Electrical Machines: Section 5 has no subject labels; the section is the subject (its machine types are kept as labelled topics)
_editorial.Power Systems: Section 6 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Control Systems: Section 7 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Electrical and Electronic Measurements: Section 8 has no subject labels; the section is the subject
_editorial.Analog Electronics: Section 9 ('Analog and Digital Electronics') split in two so analytics separate them: diode circuits, amplifiers, oscillators, op-amps, filters, VCOs/timers, Schmitt triggers, sample and hold
_editorial.Digital Electronics: Section 9 split: combinatorial/sequential logic, multiplexers, demultiplexers, A/D and D/A converters
_editorial.Power Electronics: Section 10 has no subject labels; the section is the subject

Calculus: Evaluation of definite and improper integrals
Differential Equations: Higher order linear differential equations with constant coefficients

Electric Circuits: Network Elements: Ideal voltage and current sources
Network solution methods: KCL, KVL, Node and Mesh analysis
Network Theorems: Thevenin’s, Norton’s, Superposition and Maximum Power Transfer theorem
Transient response of DC and AC networks
complex power and power factor in AC circuits

Electromagnetic Fields: Electric field and potential due to point, line, plane and spherical charge distributions
Self and Mutual inductance of simple configurations

Signals and Systems: Representation of continuous and discrete time signals
linear time invariant and causal systems
Fourier series representation of continuous and discrete time periodic signals
Applications of Fourier Transform for continuous and discrete time signals
R.M.S. value, average value calculation for any general periodic waveform

Electrical Machines: Single phase transformer: equivalent circuit, phasor diagram, open circuit and short circuit tests, regulation and efficiency
Three-phase transformers: connections, vector groups, parallel operation
DC machines: separately excited, series and shunt, motoring and generating mode of operation and their characteristics, speed control of dc motors
Three-phase induction machines: principle of operation, types, performance, torque-speed characteristics, no-load and blocked-rotor tests, equivalent circuit, starting and speed control
Operating principle of single-phase induction motors
Synchronous machines: cylindrical and salient pole machines, performance and characteristics, regulation and parallel operation of generators, starting of synchronous motors
Types of losses and efficiency calculations of electric machines

Power Systems: Basic concepts of electrical power generation
Models and performance of transmission lines and cables
Economic Load Dispatch (with and without considering transmission losses)
Gauss- Seidel and Newton-Raphson load flow methods
Principles of over‐current, differential, directional and distance protection

Control Systems: Mathematical modelling and representation of systems
Block diagrams and Signal flow graphs
Transient and Steady‐state analysis of linear time invariant systems
Stability analysis using Routh-Hurwitz and Nyquist criteria
Solution of state equations of LTI systems

Electrical and Electronic Measurements: Measurement of voltage, current, power, energy and power factor

Analog Electronics: Simple diode circuits: clipping, clamping, rectifiers
Amplifiers: biasing, equivalent circuit and frequency response

Power Electronics: Static V-I characteristics and firing/gating circuits for Thyristor, MOSFET, IGBT
DC to DC conversion: Buck, Boost and Buck-Boost Converters
Single and three-phase configuration of uncontrolled rectifiers
Voltage and Current commutated Thyristor based converters
Bidirectional ac to dc voltage source converters
Magnitude and Phase of line current harmonics for uncontrolled and thyristor based converters
Power factor and Distortion Factor of AC to DC converters
Single-phase and three-phase voltage and current source inverters
